title: Le Plan-de-la-Tour, hamlets, blue granite and shaded squares
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: Le Plan-de-la-Tour stands out through its hamlets, its squares and its geological substance. Blue granite, woodland and dispersed settlement give the village a very particular tone.
content:
Le Plan-de-la-Tour feels calm from the moment you arrive, yet that impression comes from a precise structure: an older fortified village, shaded squares, many hamlets and a landscape in which stone and woodland still carry weight.

A village that keeps the rhythm of its hamlets

Le Plan-de-la-Tour is not reduced to its centre. The hamlets matter greatly in the way the commune is read. They spread the settlement, stretch the routes and maintain a very clear relation between village and countryside.

Blue granite gives the landscape its substance

Stone is not a detail here. Blue granite affects the colour of the soils, the walls and the overall tone of the landscape. It contributes strongly to the sector’s singularity within the Maures.

Shaded squares as the centre of gravity

Even when one moves out towards the hamlets, the village keeps its centre of gravity in its squares and tree alignments. This simplicity forms much of the charm of Le Plan-de-la-Tour.
